title: Building LinkedIn's GenAI Platform — Xiaofeng Wang
talk_summary: LinkedIn's GenAI platform lead describes how they incrementally built a centralized platform (Python SDK over LangChain, prompt source-of-truth, memory layers, skill registry, observability) to bridge AI and product engineers.

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat prompts like model parameters: a dedicated submodule versions prompts and structures meta-prompts so changes are reviewed and rollback-able rather than edited live.
takeaways.evidence_quote: prompt in some way is like a traditional model parameters you want to have a really robust systems to Version Control your prompt

takeaways.technique: Centralized skill registry for agent-callable APIs
takeaways.what_they_do: Developers publish APIs into a central registry that handles skill discovery and invocation, so agents call a uniform interface instead of bespoke integrations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a set of tools uh to help our developers to publish their API into this centralized skill registry

takeaways.what_they_do: Built in-house telemetry on top of OpenTelemetry capturing low-level granularity so agent calls can be replayed, plus an analytics layer to guide optimization.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we build our in-house Solution on top of the hotel to keep track very low level granularity of the uh telary data so we can use this data to replay the uh agent call

takeaways.technique: Reuse existing messaging infra as memory layer
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than build new storage, they used LinkedIn's messaging infrastructure as the memory layer, calling it cost-efficient and scalable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: leveraging our uh messaging infrastructure uh to be as a memory layer uh is both cost efficient and scalable

takeaways.what_they_do: Organize memory into working, long-term, and collective layers and inject only relevant retrieved content into the final prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we also organize this memory into different layers including the um working memory long-term memory Collective memories

takeaways.technique: Incremental platform growth from immediate need
takeaways.what_they_do: Started with a simple Python orchestration library and grew components only as needs appeared, rather than building the full platform upfront.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of trying to build this full-fledged the platform at the beginning try to solve immediate need
